 Judgment

The plaintiffs have filed this suit seeking the relief of permanent injunction restraining the defendant or any person claiming through said defendant from dispossessing them from the plaint schedule property and also from causing unlawful interferences in their peaceful possession and enjoyment of the plaint schedule property.

The plaint averments in brief are that :
The schedule property is described as a vacant Site bearing House List No. 157/4, formed in Sy.No.212/4, Khata No.195, measuring East - West 50 feet and North - South 40 feet, totally 2,000 sq.ft. situated at Banasawadi Village, K.R.Puram Hobli, Bengaluru South taluk which is more fully described under the schedule annexed to the plaint.

The defendant herein has filed a suit in O.S.No.2785/1994 against Smt.Muniyamma W/o. Gurappa and Smt.Nagamma D/o. Late Gurappa before CCH- 8 seeking the relief of specific performance and other reliefs.
During the pendency of the said suit, the defendant No.2 has expired and her LRs have been brought on record.
The said suit ended in compromise decree between the defendant herein who was plaintiff therein and the plaintiffs herein who were defendants therein.

As per the said compromise decree, schedule 'B'
property described in the plaint in O.S.No.2785/1994 which is described as first schedule property in the compromise petition, is the House List No.157/4 which is the plaint schedule property herein.

As per the compromise petition in the said suit / 4 / O.S.No.7473/2019 in O.S.No.2785/1994, the plaintiffs herein who were defendants therein have retained the plaint schedule property and they are in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the same as its absolute owner till today as on the date of the suit.
The defendant No.1 in the said suit who is grandmother of plaintiffs herein has expired on 15.10.2015 leaving behind the plaintiffs herein as her only surviving legal heirs.
The legal heir 2(c) in the said suit by name Sri.Lokesh has also expired on 31.10.2008 leaving behind the plaintiffs herein as his only surviving legal heirs.
They both have died intestate.

The defendant who has no manner of right, title and interest in or over the plaint schedule property is trying to interfere with plaintiff's possession therein by attempting to put up stone pillars as a fencing to the said property.

The plaintiffs have lodged a complaint with the jurisdictional police who did not take any action O.S./7473/2019 on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81632957/
2 against defendant and advised the plaintiffs to work out their remedy by approaching the Civil Court.
On 29.9.2019, the defendant has attempted to put up stone pillars, who owns the land adjoining the plaint schedule property towards western side.

The plaintiffs have resisted the / 5 /
O.S.No.7473/2019 said illegal acts of the defendant.
The defendant went away by saying that he know how to put up fencing to the schedule property and he would come with more men and materials.

The said defendant is politically and financially very influential person and as such there is every possibility that he may dispossess the plaintiffs high handedly or cause unlawful interference in the plaintiff's possession of the schedule property.
Therefore, the plaintiffs having left with no other alternative have constrained to file this suit seeking the relief of permanent injunction against defendant.

3. In response to the service of summons, the defendant has entered his appearance through Sri.H.Nagaraja, the learned counsel and filed his written statement in defence to this suit of the plaintiff.
The defendant has denied in toto the entire material plaint averments in his written statement.

The said defendant has taken up contentions that, the plaintiffs had executed an Agreement of sale dated 16.10.1991 agreeing to sell the land in / 6 / O.S.No.7473/2019 Sy.No.212/4 measuring to an extent of 17 guntas where the schedule property is located and land in Sy.No.330/1A, Khata No.195 measuring 20 guntas for Rs. 1,25,000/- and received the said entire sale consideration amount from defendant.

But however, the entire land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 17 guntas was sold by Late Gurappa in favour of one Chikkairappa and his brother Hanumanthappa @ Gundappa both sons of Chinnaiah by regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961.
This fact was not disclosed to the defendant while entering into the Agreement of Sale dated 16.10.1991.
The plaintiffs predecessors did not have any right to execute the said Agreement of Sale dated 16.10.1991 in favour of defendant.
They have cheated the defendant.
Further, the plaintiffs knowing full well the aforesaid sale transaction of the year 1961 have entered into a compromise with the defendant in O.S.No.2785/1994 before CCH-8.
Therefore, the said compromise decree is illegal as both parties have acquired no manner of rights thereunder.
Neither the plaintiffs nor the defendant are in possession of the plaint schedule property after the sale in the year 1961.

The defendant came to know about the sale of 1961 / 7 /
O.S.No.7473/2019 after obtaining certified copy by which time the compromise decree was already drawn in the aforesaid suit.

The said compromise between the plaintiffs and defendant is without possession of the property and as such the present suit filed by the plaintiffs seeking injunction based on the said compromise decree is maintainable and liable to be dismissed in limine.
It is false to contend that plaintiffs were in possession of the schedule property even prior to compromise decree passed in O.S.No.2785/1994.
The said fact has to be explained by the purchasers under the regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961 who are not parties to the said compromise decree.
It is false that the defendant has tried to put up stone pillars as a fencing to the schedule property which was purchased by the purchasers under regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961.
The plaintiffs have no locus standi to file this suit as they have lost their right in the year 1961 itself over the plaint schedule property.

The mother and grandmother of plaintiffs filed a suit in O.S.No.7222/1991 before CCH-17 for declaration and injunction in respect of land bearing Sy.No.212/4 measuring 17 guntas against Assistant / 8 / O.S.No.7473/2019 Commissioner, which came to be dismissed on 27.8.1997.

In the said suit, it was decided that the possession of the entire land in Sy.No.212/4 was taken over by the O.S./7473/2019 on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81632957/
3 BDA on 20.8.1982.
In the said suit also, the sale transactions of the year 1961 was not brought to the notice of the Court.
There is no cause of action arisen to the plaintiffs to file this suit.
The cause of action one averred in the plaint is imaginary one.
This suit is bad without arraying the purchasers regd.
Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961.
The plaintiffs are entitled to none of the reliefs prayed for in this suit.
On these and certain other grounds, the defendant has prayed for dismissing the suit of the plaintiffs with costs.

4. On the strength of respective pleadings and documents of the parties, this Court has framed the following issues :
(1) Whether the plaintiffs prove that, they are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as on the date of the suit ?
/ 9 / O.S.No.7473/2019 (2) Whether the plaintiffs prove that the defendant is trying interfere with their peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property ?
(3) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled for the relief of permanent injunction against the defendant ?
(4) What Order or Decree?
5.
In order to prove the case, the plaintiffs have got examined the plaintiff No.2 as P.W.1 and relied upon in all sixteen documents marked at Exs.P.1 to P.16 and closed their side.

By way of rebuttal, the defendant has got examined himself as D.W.1 and relied upon in all eight documents marked at Exs.D.1 to D.8 and closed his side.
6.

I have heard SriChandrashekhariah, the learned counsel for the plaintiffs and Sri.H.Nagaraja, the learned counsel for the defendant.
/ 10 / O.S.No.7473/2019 7.

My findings to the above issues are as under:
 ISSUE NO.1 TO 3 : In the negative.
ISSUE NO.4 :
As per final order passed below  for the following:
REASONS
As these issues are interlinked with each other, I take them at one stretch for my consideration and determination to avoid repetition of facts.

The subject matter of this suit is a vacant land bearing House List No.167/4 carved out in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village measuring East - West 50 feet and North - South 40 feet totally 2,000 sq.ft. which is fully described under the schedule annexed to the plaint.

It is not in dispute between the parties that, originally one M.Gurappa S/o. Muniswamy was original owner and possessor of land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring to an extent of 19 guntas including 2 guntas of kharab land along with another land in Sy.No.330/1, measuring 1 acre 20 guntas having purchased the same under regd. Sale Deed dated 13.7.1955.
The / 11 / O.S.No.7473/2019 plaintiffs have produced certified copy of the said regd. Sale Deed dated 13.7.1955 as per Ex.P.1.

The plaintiffs claim that, the wife of said original owner M.Gurappa by name Smt.Muniyamma @ Munikenchamma and her daughter by name Smt.Nagamma have agreed to sell the land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas of Banasawadi Village in favour of defendant herein under Agreement of Sale dated 16.10.1991 and based on the said agreement, the defendant filed a suit in O.S.No.2785/1994 against the said vendors seeking specific performance of said agreement of sale before CCH-8 and the parties therein entered into a compromise and the said suit came to be decreed on 22.12.2006 in terms of the said compromise petition.

According to plaintiffs, the defendants in the said suit who were Smt.Muniyamma and the legal heirs of her daughter Smt.Nagamma have retained the schedule property herein to an extent of 2000 sq.ft. out of 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212/4 for themselves and since then, they are in physical possession and enjoyment of the said property.

According to plaintiffs, they are the only surviving legal heirs of / 12 / O.S.No.7473/2019 Smt.Muniyamma and her daughter Smt.Nagamma who had expired and as such they continued to be in possession and enjoyment of the plaint schedule property till today as on the date of the suit.
Per contra, the defendant has taken up two main contentions.

His first contention is that, the original owner M.Gurappa has sold the entire 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village in favour of one Chikka Irappa and his brother Hanumanthappa @ Gundappa by executing a Regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961.

His second contention is that, after the said sale transaction of the year 1961, Bangalore Development Authority has acquired and taken possession of the said entire 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212 of Banasawadi Village to form a layout by initiating acquisition proceedings.

According to defendant, when the original owner Gurappa has sold the entire 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212/4 under regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961, neither the plaintiffs' predecessors in title nor the present plaintiffs have got any manner of right, title and interest / 13 /
O.S.No.7473/2019 in or over the said Sy.No.212/4 much less over the plaint schedule property which is carved in said Sy.No.212/4 and as such the compromise decree obtained in O.S.No.2785/1994 is illegal and void and based on the said compromise decree, the plaintiffs cannot be in lawful possession of the plaint schedule property and therefore, the present suit is liable to be dismissed.

It is yet another contention of the defendant that, when the Bangalore Development Authority has acquired the entire 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village to form layout by initiating acquisition proceedings and taken over the possession of the said land on 20.8.1982 itself, the plaintiffs cannot be held to be in possession of the plaint schedule property at any point of time after the date 20.8.1982 and therefore, the present suit is liable to be dismissed.
9.

As can be seen from Ex.D.1 which is certified copy of the regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961, the original owner Gurappa had sold the entire land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas including 2 guntas of kharab land of Banasawadi Village in favour of Chikka Irappa and his brother O.S./7473/2019 on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81632957/
5 Hanumanthappa @ / 14 / O.S.No.7473/2019 Gundappa S/o. Chinnaianavar for valuable consideration of Rs.6,00/- by executing the said regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961.
This regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961 supports the testimony of D.W.1 that, the original owner Gurappa had sold the entire land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village long back in the year 1961 itself.

The next contention of the defendant is that, after this sale transaction of the year 1961, the Bangalore Development Authority has acquired the said entire land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas for formation of layout by initiating acquisition proceedings.

Exs. D.2 and D.3 are certified copies of the Preliminary and Final Notifications dated 3.11.1977 and 13.11.1980 respectively published in the Mysore Gazette for acquisition of the various lands of Banasawadi Village for formation of the layout by the Bangalore Development Authority.

As can be seen at Sl.No.114 of Preliminary Notification dated 3.11.1977 issued under Section 17 of the B.D.A. Act, 1970 in Ex.D.3, the name of the purchaser viz., Sri.M.Gundappa S/o.Muniswamy is reflected as owner of the land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas proposed to be acquired under the said / 15 / O.S.No.7473/2019 notification by the B.D.A.

The said name of purchaser viz., Sri.M.Gundappa S/o. Muniswamy is also reflected as owner of the land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas acquired in the final notification dated 13.11.1980 issued under Section 19 of the B.D.A. Act, 1970 for formation of the layout called "Banasawadi Scheme between Old Madras Road and Banasawadi Road".

The reflection of purchaser's name viz.,M.Gundappa S/o.Muniswamy in the aforesaid preliminary and Final Notifications fortifies the contention of the defendant that the said land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas was sold by original owner Gurappa under regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961.
It is on the strength of the said regd.
Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961,

the name of said Sri.M.Gundappa S/o.Muniswamy has been shown as owner of the acquired land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village in the aforesaid Preliminary and Final Notifications marked at Exs.D.3 and D.4 respectively.

Further, Ex.D.6 discloses that, after issuance of notification under Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, while taking possession of the 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village by the B.D.A., there was / 16 /
O.S.No.7473/2019 mahazar drawn in the presence of SLAO and elderly persons of Banasawadi Village by the Taluka Surveyor on 20.8.1982.

This Ex.D.6 - Mahazar drawn by the Taluka Surveyor coupled with the issuance of notification under Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, discloses that the B.D.A. has acquired the land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas by initiating acquisition proceedings and passing Award for compensation to the owner and thereafter it has also taken possession of the said land in Sy.No.212/4 for formation of layout.
As per Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, the issuance of the notification under Section 16 itself is a conclusive evidence of taking possession of the acquired land.

It is worth to note that, pursuant to aforesaid acquisition proceedings, the name of B.D.A. came to be mutated in the revenue records of land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village by certification of mutation entry MR.No.1/1990-91.
The defendant has produced several RTC extracts of said Sy.No. 212/4 of Banasawadi Village which are marked together as Ex.D.5.

As can be seen from the said RTC extracts, the name of B.D.A. finds a place in kabjedar's column No.9 and cultivator's column No.12 / 17 / O.S.No.7473/2019 as owner and cultivator of the land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village for the period 2018-19 to till the date of year of filing of this suit.

It is to note that, the wife and daughter of original owner Gurappa viz.,
Smt.Muniyamma and Smt. Nagamma had filed a suit in O.S.No.7222/1991 before the then II Addl.
City Civil Judge, Bengaluru (CCH-17) against the Commissioner, Bangalore Development Authority and Assistant Commissioner, Bengaluru seeking the relief of declaration that the aforesaid Preliminary Notification dated 3.11.1977 as per Ex.D.3 and Final Notification dated 13.11.1980 as per O.S./7473/2019 on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81632957/
6 Ex.D.4 have rendered themselves infructuous and inoperative and for the consequential relief of injunction.

City Civil Judge, Bengaluru (CCH-17)

sentences.text: The said suit came to be dismissed by its Judgment and Decree dated 27.8.1997.
The defendant has produced the certified copy of the said Judgment and Decree as per Ex.D.7.
It therefore clear that, the predecessors of the plaintiffs herein had challenged the aforesaid acquisition proceedings and suffered decree in the hands of the Civil Court.

Thus, all these above documentary evidence discussed herein supra, very clearly demonstrates that, the original owner Gurappa had sold the / 18 / O.S.No.7473/2019 entire land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas in favour of two brothers by name Chikka Irappa and Hanumanthappa @ Gundappa under Regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961 and
thereafter, the B.D.A. had acquired and taken possession of the said 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village by initiating acquisition proceedings.

Accordingly the said land in Sy.No.212/4 measuring 19 guntas now stands in the name of B.D.A.
since the date of taking possession on 20.8.1982 till today as on the date of the suit.

The facts elicited on the record being stood thus, the claim of the plaintiff that, they are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the plaint schedule property since the time of their predecessor in title based on the compromise decree passed in O.S.No.2785/1994 dated 22.12.2006, cannot be countenanced.

As rightly contended by the defendant, the original owner Gurappa or his wife Smt.Muniyamma or their daughter Smt.Nagamma did not have any right over the land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village so as to enter into an Agreement of sale dated 16.10.1991 agreeing to sell the said land in favour of defendant herein since the said original owner Gurappa had sold / 19 / O.S.No.7473/2019 the said land under regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961 and thereafter, B.D.A. has acquired the said land for formation of layout by initiating acquisition proceedings.

Therefore, it automatically follows that,
the compromise decree dated 22.12.2006 in O.S.No.2785/1994 was obtained by the plaintiffs and their predecessors by practicing fraud upon the Court by suppressing the material facts.

Therefore,
the said compromise decree is a nullity in the eye of law.

Neither the plaintiffs nor the defendant can claim possession over the plaint schedule property based on the said compromise decree dated 22.12.2006 passed in O.S.No.2785/1994 as the land in question was stood vested in the ownership and possession of B.D.A. much prior to the filing of the said suit in O.S.No.2785/1994.

The said decree is a collusive decree obtained behind the back and without the knowledge of B.D.A. Such being the case, I am of the considered opinion that the plaintiffs cannot be in lawful possession of the plaint schedule property unless it is shown or established that the plaintiffs have dispossessed the B.D.A. from the plaint schedule property at any point of time after the date 20.8.1982.
/ 20 / O.S.No.7473/2019

When the plaintiffs cannot be held to be in lawful possession of the plaint schedule property, the question of causing unlawful obstructions or interferences in their such possession by defendant does not arise at all.

When the plaintiffs cannot be in lawful possession of the plaint schedule property and when there is no question of causing interferences in their such possession by anybody including defendant, it also automatically follows that the plaintiffs are not entitled to the relief of permanent injunction as prayed for in this suit.

With these observations, I shall conclude my discussion with the following conclusions :
(a) The plaintiffs have failed to prove that they are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the plaint schedule property as on the date of the suit.
Accordingly, the Issue No.1 framed herein above is answered in the negative against the plaintiffs.

O.S./7473/2019 on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81632957/
7

(b) When the plaintiffs have failed to prove their lawful possession in the plaint schedule property as on the date of suit, the question of illegal interferences in plaintiffs' such possession of the schedule property by defendant does not arise at all.
/ 21 / O.S.No.7473/2019 Hence, I am of the opinion that the plaintiffs have also failed to prove the illegal interferences in their alleged possession of the plaint schedule property from defendant.
Accordingly, the Issue No.2 framed herein above is answered in the negative against the plaintiffs.

(c) When the plaintiffs have failed to prove their lawful possession in the plaint schedule property and illegal interferences in their such possession from defendant, it automatically follows that the plaintiffs are entitled to none of the reliefs sought for in the plaint.
Accordingly, the Issue No.3 framed herein above is answered in the negative against the plaintiffs.
10. ISSUE NO.4

In view of my findings given on Issue No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed herein above paragraphs, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiffs is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw up decree accordingly.

(Dictated to the Judgment Writer, typed directly on computer, script corrected,
signed and then pronounced by me in the open court, this the 17th day of April,
2023.)

(YASHAWANT R TAWARE) XXXIX Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge,
Bangalore City.

According to plaintiffs, the defendants in the said suit who were Smt.Muniyamma and the legal heirs of her daughter Smt.Nagamma have retained the schedule property herein to an extent of 2000 sq.ft. out of 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212/4 for themselves and since then, they are in physical possession and enjoyment of the said property.
According to defendant, when the original owner Gurappa has sold the entire 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.212/4 under regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961, neither the plaintiffs' predecessors in title nor the present plaintiffs have got any manner of right, title and interest / 13 /
O.S.No.7473/2019 in or over the said Sy.No.212/4 much less over the plaint schedule property which is carved in said Sy.No.212/4 and as such the compromise decree obtained in O.S.No.2785/1994 is illegal and void and based on the said compromise decree, the plaintiffs cannot be in lawful possession of the plaint schedule property and therefore, the present suit is liable to be dismissed.
The said suit came to be dismissed by its Judgment and Decree dated 27.8.1997.
The facts elicited on the record being stood thus, the claim of the plaintiff that, they are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the plaint schedule property since the time of their predecessor in title based on the compromise decree passed in O.S.No.2785/1994 dated 22.12.2006, cannot be countenanced.
As rightly contended by the defendant, the original owner Gurappa or his wife Smt.Muniyamma or their daughter Smt.Nagamma did not have any right over the land in Sy.No.212/4 of Banasawadi Village so as to enter into an Agreement of sale dated 16.10.1991 agreeing to sell the said land in favour of defendant herein since the said original owner Gurappa had sold / 19 / O.S.No.7473/2019 the said land under regd. Sale Deed dated 15.7.1961 and thereafter, B.D.A. has acquired the said land for formation of layout by initiating acquisition proceedings.
Therefore, it automatically follows that,
the compromise decree dated 22.12.2006 in O.S.No.2785/1994 was obtained by the plaintiffs and their predecessors by practicing fraud upon the Court by suppressing the material facts.
Therefore,
the said compromise decree is a nullity in the eye of law.
Neither the plaintiffs nor the defendant can claim possession over the plaint schedule property based on the said compromise decree dated 22.12.2006 passed in O.S.No.2785/1994 as the land in question was stood vested in the ownership and possession of B.D.A. much prior to the filing of the said suit in O.S.No.2785/1994.
The said decree is a collusive decree obtained behind the back and without the knowledge of B.D.A. Such being the case, I am of the considered opinion that the plaintiffs cannot be in lawful possession of the plaint schedule property unless it is shown or established that the plaintiffs have dispossessed the B.D.A. from the plaint schedule property at any point of time after the date 20.8.1982.
/ 20 / O.S.No.7473/2019
When the plaintiffs cannot be held to be in lawful possession of the plaint schedule property, the question of causing unlawful obstructions or interferences in their such possession by defendant does not arise at all.
When the plaintiffs cannot be in lawful possession of the plaint schedule property and when there is no question of causing interferences in their such possession by anybody including defendant, it also automatically follows that the plaintiffs are not entitled to the relief of permanent injunction as prayed for in this suit.
